issue.title: Automatically append ellipsis (`...`) to metavars when `multiple=True` in options

relevant_locations.role: The Option class where make_metavar should be overridden to append an ellipsis when multiple=True.
The method that calls self.make_metavar(ctx=ctx) to format the option's help record.

llm_context.input_title: Automatically append ellipsis (`...`) to metavars when `multiple=True` in options
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: When a command-line option is configured with `multiple=True`, the auto-generated help text does not visually indicate that the option can be repeated. This issue proposes automatically appending an ellipsis (`...`) to the option's metavar (e.g., changing `--foo TEXT` to `--foo TEXT...`) to follow standard CLI conventions for repeatable options.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The `Option` class in `src/click/core.py` does not override the `make_metavar` method from `Parameter`. When `Option.get_help_record` formats the option's help record, it calls `self.make_metavar(ctx=ctx)`. Because there is no option-specific implementation, it falls back to the default `Parameter.make_metavar` which does not append an ellipsis for `multiple=True`. In contrast, `Argument` overrides `make_metavar` to append `...` when `self.nargs != 1`.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect Option and Parameter classes in src/click/core.py
step_by_step_plan.description: Examine the `Option` class and its parent `Parameter` class in `src/click/core.py`. Note how `Parameter.make_metavar` generates the default metavar and how `Option.get_help_record` uses it.

step_by_step_plan.title: Override make_metavar in Option class
step_by_step_plan.description: Implement `make_metavar` in the `Option` class in `src/click/core.py`. It should call `super().make_metavar(ctx)` to get the base metavar, and if `self.multiple` is `True` and the metavar is not empty, append `...` to it.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: A placeholder string (such as TEXT, INT, or PATH) used in command-line help menus to represent the expected type or format of an option or argument value.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Metavars guide users on what kind of input a command expects, making the command-line interface self-documenting and user-friendly.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The issue requires modifying the metavar of an Option to append '...' when the option accepts multiple values, visually indicating repeatability to the user.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: An object-oriented programming technique where a subclass provides a specific implementation of a method that is already defined in its superclass.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: It allows specialized behavior for subclasses (like Option or Argument) while reusing common logic from the base class (Parameter).
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Option needs to override make_metavar from Parameter to add custom behavior (appending '...' for multiple options) while still leveraging the base class's metavar generation logic via super().make_metavar(ctx).

common_pitfalls: Modifying Parameter.make_metavar directly, which might affect other parameter types (like Argument) in unintended ways or cause duplicate ellipses.
Forgetting to call super().make_metavar(ctx) inside the overridden Option.make_metavar, which would break custom metavars or default metavar resolution.
Appending '...' multiple times if make_metavar is called repeatedly or if multiple is checked incorrectly.
